title: AnalysisJobStarted
description: Worker → Platform runtime signal: the worker DEQUEUED a job and began processing it. Published to the direct queue `analysis_job_started` (exchange=""), the same one-way path as `analysis_results` — the worker never calls the platform back over HTTP (KR-070/KR-071). WHY THIS EXISTS: the platform's analysis_jobs state machine only accepts complete() from PROCESSING, and until this signal existed nothing could ever put a job into PROCESSING — every job stayed PENDING forever, so 'queued for 2 days' and 'running right now' were indistinguishable. Deliberately PII-free: no field_id, no owner, no coordinates.

job_id.description: Job identifier. Same dual form as analysis_job.v1 (worker runtime UUID, orchestration job_<24hex>) so the platform can key on it without translation.

status.description: Constant. Present so the wire is self-describing and the consumer can assert on it instead of inferring meaning from the queue name.

started_at.description: When the worker began processing (ISO 8601 UTC). Becomes analysis_jobs.started_at.

worker_version.description: Worker application version that picked the job up. Lets a stuck job be attributed to a specific deployed build.

contracts_version.description: Contract set version the worker is pinned to (I-1). A start signal from a worker on an older pin is the earliest observable symptom of a version-alignment break.

attempt.description: 1 on first delivery, higher on RabbitMQ redelivery. The consumer MUST treat a repeated start for the same job as idempotent — a redelivered job is not an error.
